en: Now I mentioned and showed it before that
balancing is done with help of so-called
balance factors.
Balance factors are simply the difference
between the subtree depths and we can, for
example, derive them by subtracting the
right subtree depth from the left subtree
depth.
Therefore, for example, on this first
top-left binary search tree,
these would be our balance factors for the
individual nodes.
The topmost node, the root node, has a
balance factor of -2 because it has no left
branch. It only has a right branch with a
depth of 2. So the right branch depth from
node 1's perspective is 2.
The left branch's depth from node 1's
perspective is 0.
0 minus 2 is
-2, so that would be the balance factor of
1. Now if we step down further into the
tree, that picture changes. For the next
node with the value 2,
we have a right branch depth of 1 because we
have 1 child node there,
and we have a left branch depth of 0, so we
have a balance factor of -1 on that level.
And that is fine, we don't need to swap
anything around there, which is why we only
need 1 rotation here to end up with our
balanced tree where we always have 0 as a
factor because from the root node's
perspective, which is the node with value 2,
the right branch depth is 1 and the left
branch depth is 1, and 1 minus 1 is 0. And
the same is true for the leaf nodes.
Now in the next example here, this would be
our balance factors, basically the same just
in the opposite direction. That's why we
don't have negative numbers here.
And now for the bottom left case,
there, this would be our
balance factors.
And here we need 2 rotations even though, of
course, the node with value 1
has a balance factor of
-1, which theoretically would be okay. A
difference of 1 is okay,
but we still need to balance this out.
Otherwise, we'll have no way of fixing the
balance factor of 2 on the root node. That's
why we make this first transformation so
that we end up with these balance factors
and then we can finally all set them to 0 by
making one additional transformation here.
And in the bottom right corner, we therefore
basically have the opposite.
Now, these are the balance factors. They
play a crucial role because they help us
determine which kind of rotation we need to
perform
and therefore an AVL tree is really about
that. It's about calculating those balance
factors for every node and then about doing
those rotations.
And obviously, as you can imagine, typically
your trees will not just have 3 values. So
of course we need to make sure that the
entire tree is balanced out and not just the
first 3 nodes.
